newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rail reform plan gets key senator backing.
newsitem.headline: French rail reform plan gets key senator backing.

text.p: A French senator advising on the SNCF state railways gave his backing to a rail reform package on Wednesday and said legislation on the reform would be pushed through parliament under urgency procedures.
The reform plan involves spinning off 134.2 billion francs in debt, out of 208 billion, to a new state holding company which would in turn become owner of the rail infrastructure.

The two largest unions in the SNCF, the Communist-led CGT and the Socialist CFDT, are opposed to the reform on the grounds it amounts to a break-up and could open the way to competition on the network.

"Even it it will still be left with a hefty debt, the SNCF can now take care of itself," Gerbaud told reporters when presenting his report on the matter. The reform requires legislation to create the new state firm that will take over the debts and charge SNCF fees for use of the infrastructure.

The bill, put on hold by Transport Minister Bernard Pons late last year amid union disquiet, has been resuscitated after a government decision to raise the amount of debt being spun off from the 125 billion francs originally envisaged.
"It will all go very quickly," said Gerbaud. The bill goes to the Senate for examination from January 21 to 23.
The new infrastructure company will be called France Rail.
